## QUESTION 2

__What year had the most babies named 'David'? How many babies were named 'David' that year?__

The year that had the most babies born with the name "David" was: 1955
There were 86389 babies named "David" born in that year.

```{python}
# Q2

'''
I need to:
[x] only have rows where the name is David
[x] then add together the # born in each year (Which is already done in the data set as total)
[x] take the year with the most of them

[x] print the year and the number.
'''

answerA = df.filter(pl.col("name") == "David").sort("Total", descending=True)["year"][0]

answerB = df.filter(pl.col("name") == "David", "year").select("Total").max().item()


print(f'The year that had the most babies born with the name "David" was: {answerA}')
print(f'There were {answerB} babies named "David" born in that year.')

```


## QUESTION 3

__What year did your name hit its peak? How many babies were named your name in that year?__

My name (Justin) hit its peak in 1988
In that year there were 35243 babies born with my name.

```{python}
# Q3

answerA = df.filter(pl.col("name") == "Justin").sort("Total", descending=True)["year"][0]

answerB = df.filter(pl.col("name") == "Justin", "year").select("Total").max().item()

print(f'My name (Justin) hit its peak in {answerA}\nIn that year there were {answerB} babies born with my name.')

```


## QUESTION 4

__In the most recent year, what was the most common female name in Utah?__ 

In the dataset, the most recent year is 2015, and in that year, the most common name is Emma which was given to 281 number of female babies. 

```{python}
# Q5
'''

- Get a dataframe with 'name', 'year', female/male, 'count', 'UT'

[x] Locate data 
[x] Clean data if needed
[x] Load new data frame
[x] Remove any row when 'Sex' is 'M'
[x] Remove any row when 'StateCode' is not 'UT'
[x] Find the .max of 'YearOfBirth'
[x] Sort by highest 'Number' (name count)
[x] display the results
'''

# Load new data frame
df_new = pl.read_csv("babyNamesUS.csv")

# Remove any row when 'Sex' is 'M'
df_new = df_new.filter(pl.col('Sex') == 'F')

# Remove any row when 'StateCode' is not 'UT'
df_new = df_new.filter(pl.col('StateCode') == 'UT') 

# Find the .max of 'YearOfBirth'
# Find what year it is
max_year = df_new.select(pl.col("YearOfBirth").max()).item()
# Exculde all other entries
df_new = df_new.filter(pl.col("YearOfBirth") == max_year)

# Sort by highest 'Number' (name count)
df_new = df_new.sort('Number', descending=True)

# Print it all out!
print(f'In the dataset, the most recent year is {max_year}, and in that year, the most common name is {df_new.head(1)['Name'].item()} which was given to {df_new.head(1)["Number"].item()} number of female babies.')

```
